purpose: Naldemedine is used to treat constipation caused by opioid pain medications in adults with chronic non-cancer pain. It helps get your bowels moving again when opioids like morphine or oxycodone are slowing down your digestive system. It is not meant to treat general constipation unrelated to opioid use.
how_it_works: Opioid pain medicines can block the normal movement of your intestines, which causes constipation. Naldemedine works by blocking opioid receptors specifically in your gut, essentially telling your intestines to start working normally again. The good news is it stays mostly in the digestive system, so it does not block the pain-relieving effects of your opioid medication.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach pain, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting. These usually happen because your digestive system is waking back up and getting active again. Let your doctor know if diarrhea becomes severe or does not go away.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have a blockage in your stomach or intestines. If you have a history of certain stomach conditions like Crohn's disease or diverticulitis, talk to your doctor first because there is a small risk of a tear in the intestinal wall. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain, especially if it feels like something is seriously wrong. Also, it may cause opioid withdrawal symptoms in some people.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 0.2 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
